_meta: Default copy for the lifecycle emails, tokenized so the dashboard editor can edit them like the sequence emails. Token fills + fallbacks live in _lib/email-templates.ts (every token always resolves, so no line ever renders empty). KV override key: emailcopy:<template>. Copy SSOT for wording remains Plans/01_email_and_nurture/email-copy-book.md.

welcome-exercise.subject: Your first solve is saved
welcome-exercise.preheader: The XP is yours. Here's how to keep it going.
welcome-exercise.body:
Hi {first_name},

Nice work on that first exercise. It's saved to your profile now, XP and all, and your streak started today.

If you feel like doing another, the rest of that hub is open right where you left off:

[Keep practicing -> {hub_url}]

The free plan gives you 25 graded exercises a month, which is plenty to build a real habit.

Oh, and one thing I don't want you to miss: your account comes with the full Data Analyst track, free for 30 days. The clock doesn't start until you open the track, so there's no rush. It's interactive lessons rather than exercises, you learn something properly and then practice it right there in the browser. Worth a look when you're ready.

The New to R course and all the tutorials are free forever either way.

If you get stuck or something's confusing, just reply to this email and I'll help.

Akshay

welcome-lesson.subject: Pick up where you left off
welcome-lesson.preheader: Your lesson is open again, and there's more where it came from.
welcome-lesson.body:
Hi {first_name},

You're in. {course_line}

Also, and I don't think you know this yet: it's not just that one lesson. The whole Data Analyst track is free for your first 30 days, all the lessons, the quizzes, the certificate at the end. The clock starts the first time you open a lesson on the track, so it's yours to begin whenever you're ready. Once you finish the lesson that brought you here, you can just keep going.

[Continue the lesson -> {next_lesson_url}]

Whatever you complete stays completed, even after the 30 days. And the New to R course plus all the tutorials are free forever regardless.

If anything's unclear, reply and ask. I read these.

Akshay

welcome-browsing.subject: Welcome, and where I'd start
welcome-browsing.preheader: One good starting point, not a tour.
welcome-browsing.body:
Hi {first_name},

Welcome! Rather than giving you a tour of everything, let me just point you at the best thing you now have: the Data Analyst track, free for 30 days. Interactive lessons, R running right in the browser, a certificate at the end. The clock only starts when you open your first lesson, and lesson one takes about twenty minutes:

[Start lesson one -> {start_url}]

If you've never written any R at all, the New to R course might be a friendlier place to begin. That one's free forever, no time limit.

Either way, you don't need to figure the whole site out today. Start with one lesson and see how it feels.

Stuck anywhere? Just reply, it's me reading, not a bot.

Akshay

pass-23.subject: Your Data Analyst pass ends {pass_end_date}
pass-23.preheader: One week left. What stays free after, and what does not.
pass-23.body:
Hi {first_name},

A quick heads-up: your Data Analyst pass has about a week left. Until {pass_end_date} the whole track is still open to you, every lesson and every quiz.

After that it moves to Pro. You'll keep everything you finished, plus your XP and streak, and the New to R course and all the tutorials stay free like always. It's only the remaining lessons on the track that close.

So if you've been meaning to get through a few more, this is the week for it.

[Continue the track -> {next_lesson_url}]

Akshay

pass-30.subject: Last day of your Data Analyst pass
pass-30.preheader: The track closes tonight. Everything you finished stays.
pass-30.body:
Hi {first_name},

Today's the last day of your pass. At midnight UTC the Data Analyst track moves to Pro for your account.

If you're in the middle of a lesson, tonight is worth finishing it. Anything you complete stays completed forever.

[Open the track -> {next_lesson_url}]

And whatever happens tonight, your XP, your streak and the free practice all stay exactly as they are.

Akshay

pass-31.subject: Your pass ended, your progress didn't
pass-31.preheader: Everything you finished stays. Here is how things look from today.
pass-31.body:
Hi {first_name},

Your 30 days wrapped up yesterday. Before anything else, thanks for spending part of your month learning here. I mean that.

Nothing you did is lost. The lessons you finished, your XP, your streak, they're all still on your profile. The New to R course and the tutorials stay free, and you still get 25 graded practice exercises every month.

If Pro ever makes sense for you down the road, you'll pick up exactly where you stopped. Nothing resets.

And if there's anything I can help with in the meantime, you know where the reply button is.

Akshay

cap.subject: All 25 for this month, done
cap.preheader: Your started hubs stay open. A fresh 25 lands on {reset_date}.
cap.body:
Hi {first_name},

You just used your 25th graded exercise this month. Honestly, that's a serious month of practice. Most people never get close.

Nothing dramatic happens now. Every hub you started stays open until {reset_date}, lessons and tutorials aren't affected at all, and your streak and XP are safe. A fresh 25 arrives on {reset_date}.

If waiting sounds annoying, Pro removes the cap entirely:

[Have a look at Pro -> {pricing_url}]

Either way, nice work this month.

Akshay

flip.subject: Two changes to your r-statistics.co account
flip.preheader: Free practice gets a monthly allowance, and the Data Analyst track opens free for 30 days.
flip.body:
Hi {first_name},

Two changes to the free tier, live today. The short version:

Free practice now gives you 25 graded exercises a month. Any hub you start stays open until the month ends, so you won't get cut off mid-set. Lessons and tutorials aren't metered at all, and nothing you've already earned changes.

Second, and this one's the good news: the full Data Analyst track is now free for 30 days on every account, including yours. The clock starts the first time you open a lesson on the track, not today, so read this at your leisure. Whatever you finish stays finished, even after the window closes.

Why the change? Grading and hosting cost real money, and this keeps the free tier sustainable without touching what matters: New to R and all 1,300+ tutorials stay free forever.

Thirty days is enough to get real value out of that track. It's yours whenever you're ready:

[Start the Data Analyst track -> {start_url}]

Questions or objections, just reply. I answer every one.

Akshay

invite-series.subject: A daily R lesson, if you want it
invite-series.preheader: One interactive lesson a day, three days to take each one. One click to join.
invite-series.body:
Hi {first_name},

We've been building something new: a daily lesson series.

Here's how it works. Six days a week you get one short email, and each email unlocks an interactive lesson made for that day: how statistical inference works, what p-values mean, confidence intervals, ARIMA, regression health checks, and on from there. You read, you run real R code right in the browser, you answer a few quick checks, and you're done in about fifteen minutes. Each lesson stays open for three days, then the next one takes its place.

There's nothing to install and nothing to pay. These lessons aren't on the site menus at all; the emails are the only door in.

If you want in, one click does it:

[Start the daily series -> {join_url}]

Your first lesson lands in your inbox right away, and the next one arrives tomorrow. If it's not for you, do nothing and nothing changes.

Questions, just reply. I answer every one.

Akshay
